subject: microeconomics
question_text:
Country A's competitive market has inverse domestic demand P = 80 - Q and inverse domestic supply P = 20 + Q, with no externalities. P is dollars per unit and Q is units per day. Country A is small in the world market and can import the good at a constant world price of $30 per unit. Ignore transportation costs.
(a) Calculate the equilibrium price and quantity before international trade.
(b) Calculate domestic quantity demanded, domestic quantity supplied, and imports under free trade. Show your work.
(c) Country A imposes a $10 per-unit import tariff. Calculate the new domestic price and the quantity imported, and explain why imports change.
(d) Calculate the change in domestic producer surplus caused by the tariff and calculate tariff revenue. Show your work.

answer.answer_markdown:
### (a) Equilibrium before trade
Set domestic demand equal to domestic supply:

\[
80-Q=20+Q \quad\Rightarrow\quad Q=30.
\]
Substitute into either curve: \(P=50\). **Equilibrium: price $50, quantity 30 units per day.**

### (b) Free trade
The world price is $30. At that price:

- Quantity demanded: \(30=80-Q_d\Rightarrow Q_d=50\).
- Quantity supplied: \(30=20+Q_s\Rightarrow Q_s=10\).
- Imports: \(Q_d-Q_s=50-10=40\) units per day.

### (c) $10 tariff
The tariff raises the price of imports to \(30+10=\$40\). As a small country, Country A takes this tariff-inclusive price as its domestic price. At $40:

\[
Q_d=80-40=40,\qquad Q_s=40-20=20,
\]
so imports are \(40-20=20\) units per day. Imports fall from 40 to 20 because the higher domestic price reduces quantity demanded and increases domestic quantity supplied.

### (d) Producer surplus and tariff revenue
At the free-trade price of $30, producer surplus is a triangle with height \(30-20=10\) and base 10:

\[
PS_{FT}=\tfrac12(10)(10)=\$50\text{ per day}.
\]
With the tariff, producer surplus has height \(40-20=20\) and base 20:

\[
PS_T=\tfrac12(20)(20)=\$200\text{ per day}.
\]
Thus, the **change in domestic producer surplus is an increase of $150 per day**.

Tariff revenue equals the tariff per unit times imports after the tariff:

\[
TR=\$10\times20=\$200\text{ per day}.
\]

criterion_grades.evidence: At $30, calculates Qd=50, Qs=10, and imports=40, showing the calculations.
Finds tariff-inclusive domestic price $40 and imports 20; explains that the higher price lowers demand and raises domestic supply.
Calculates free-trade producer surplus $50, tariff producer surplus $200, increase $150, and tariff revenue $200 using the post-tariff imports.

answer.answer_markdown:
### (a) Before trade
Set domestic demand equal to domestic supply:
\[
80-Q=20+Q \Rightarrow Q=30,\qquad P=50.
\]
The equilibrium is **$50 per unit and 30 units per day**.

### (b) Free trade
The world price is $30. Since it is below the no-trade price, Country A imports the good.

\[
Q_d=80-30=50,\qquad Q_s=30-20=10
\]
\[
\text{Imports}=Q_d-Q_s=50-10=40.
\]
At free trade, domestic quantity demanded is **50**, domestic quantity supplied is **10**, and imports are **40 units per day**.

### (c) $10 tariff
The tariff raises the domestic price to **$40** ($30 world price + $10 tariff).

\[
Q_d=80-40=40,\qquad Q_s=40-20=20
\]
\[
\text{Imports}=40-20=20.
\]
Imports fall from 40 to 20 units per day because the higher domestic price reduces quantity demanded and increases domestic quantity supplied.

### (d) Producer surplus and tariff revenue
Domestic producers receive a price increase from $30 to $40, and output rises from 10 to 20. The increase in producer surplus is the rectangle plus triangle:
\[
\Delta PS=(10)(10)+\tfrac12(10)(10)=100+50=\boxed{\$150\text{ per day}}.
\]
Tariff revenue is the tariff per unit times imports after the tariff:
\[
TR=(\$10)(20)=\boxed{\$200\text{ per day}}.
\]

answer.answer_markdown:
### (a) Equilibrium before trade
Set domestic demand equal to domestic supply:
\[
80-Q=20+Q \quad\Rightarrow\quad Q=30.
\]
Substitute into either curve: \(P=80-30=\boxed{\$50}\). The autarky equilibrium is **30 units per day at $50 per unit**.

### (b) Free trade
The world price is $30. Since it is below the autarky price, Country A imports the good. At \(P=30\):
\[
Q_d=80-30=\boxed{50},\qquad Q_s=30-20=\boxed{10}.
\]
Imports are \(Q_d-Q_s=50-10=\boxed{40}\) units per day.

### (c) $10 tariff
The tariff raises the price of imports available domestically to \(30+10=\boxed{\$40}\). At this price, \(Q_d=80-40=40\) and \(Q_s=40-20=20\), so imports are \(40-20=\boxed{20}\) units per day. Imports fall because the higher domestic price reduces quantity demanded and increases domestic quantity supplied.

### (d) Producer surplus and tariff revenue
Before the tariff, domestic producers receive $30 and supply 10 units. Their producer surplus is
\[
PS_0=\tfrac12(30-20)(10)=\$50.
\]
After the tariff, they receive $40 and supply 20 units:
\[
PS_1=\tfrac12(40-20)(20)=\$200.
\]
Thus the change in domestic producer surplus is \(PS_1-PS_0=\boxed{+\$150\text{ per day}}\).

Tariff revenue equals the tariff per imported unit times imports after the tariff:
\[
TR=10(20)=\boxed{\$200\text{ per day}}.
\]
